Youth Core Culture · 12-week first term.

How the first term works.

Teens learn to move and work with a partner. Sandy guides each class. Try a task. Learn the rules. Build skill as you train.

What the first term includes.

Choose a weekly class plan for your family. Each plan runs for 12 weeks.

  • 1 class each week: $220
  • 2 classes each week: $440
  • 3 classes each week: $550
  • 1, 2, or 3 planned classes each week.
  • Sandy helps your teen find a partner.
  • Sandy checks what your teen learns.
  • Your first paid term comes with a uniform.
  • Class videos follow your plan terms.
  • At week 12, talk about what comes next.

First visit walkthrough.

What happens at a teen Free First Visit?

First, meet Sandy and see the room. Your teen can ask questions, learn the safety rules, and try a coached activity. A parent or guardian stays on site.

Sandy will confirm the visit plan and what to wear. See the Free First Visit steps and waiver.

Step 1.

Tour & Meet Coach Sandy.

Meet Sandy, see the room, and ask your questions.

Step 2.

Safety Rules & Matched Partner.

Learn how to tap and reset. Train with a calm partner at your own pace.

Step 3.

Guided skill work.

Test simple answers with friendly partners. Enjoy calm guidance and cooperative drills from day one.

Cross-training.

Already play a sport?

Keep playing it.

Class tasks use skills teens can bring to their sport:

  • Balance and footwork.
  • Grip and hand work.
  • Core moves and quick steps.
  • Stamina.
  • Calm focus in hard tasks.
See Athlete Cross-Training
What happens in class.

Guided partner work.

Teens learn a move, try it with a partner, and talk it over with Coach Sandy. As they learn, Sandy can help them pick a next step.

Questions parents & teens ask.

Before the first class.

Are beginners welcome?

Yes. Every student starts with simple movement, safe falling, and matched partner pacing.

What style is practiced?

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu focuses on leverage, balance, and positional control.

Can parents watch?

Yes. The studio is open and parents are always welcome to observe.
